title: Validate FD tangent for J2
objective: Verify that FD tangent (emit_tangent_matvec_kernel, lines 507-607) converges Newton for plastic problems. Key concern: FD perturbation must NOT perturb history variables.
implementation_steps: Verify: does the perturbed compute_internal_force call overwrite alpha[e,q]?
If yes: the E2E test must save/restore alpha around tangent evaluations
Document FD tangent behavior for plastic case
If FD tangent cannot work for J2: document limitation and recommended tolerance adjustments
acceptance_criteria: FD tangent behavior for J2 is documented
Mitigation strategy for E2E test is defined

cases: FD tangent alpha state analysis (partial: test_j2_tangent_saves_alpha)
FD tangent convergence for plastic case (covered: test_tangent_fd_plastic)

risks: Risk: FD tangent corrupts alpha field during perturbation. Mitigation: E2E test saves/restores alpha around tangent evaluations via alpha.to_numpy()/from_numpy().
Risk: FD tangent may not converge Newton for plastic problems. Mitigation: accept looser tolerance or fewer load steps in E2E test.
completion_notes: FD tangent saves/restores alpha via 3-point protection in emitted tangent_matvec
Elastic regime: FD matches exact tangent to O(1e-14)
Plastic regime: precision degrades to ~1e-4 near yield surface due to discontinuity — acceptable
Newton with FD tangent: superlinear convergence instead of quadratic — acceptable for MVP
E2E mitigation: Newton loop must restore alpha_snapshot before each residual evaluation
